questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify the audience of a design brief

stimulus.body: A short reference note on rhetorical situation is set for a close-reading task. It states: The review board holds safety authority, so it is the primary audience. A marginal reminder adds: ask who can say no to the design. Four statements are then offered, and only one of them follows from what the note actually says.

questions.stem: The passage above presents a case and the terms needed to judge it. Based only on what the passage establishes about rhetorical situation, which choice holds up?

options.text: The structural review board with authority over safety
The city council that approves funding and permits
options.misconception: treats a secondary stakeholder as primary

options.text: The general public who will walk across the bridge
options.misconception: confuses end users with decision makers

options.text: The contractor who will pour the concrete

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the review board holds safety authority, so it is the primary audience. On that basis "The structural review board with authority over safety" is the supported choice. Option B ("The city council that approves funding and permits") fails because it treats a secondary stakeholder as primary; Option C ("The general public who will walk across the bridge") fails because it confuses end users with decision makers; Option D ("The contractor who will pour the concrete") fails because it confuses executor with approver.
questions.hint: Ask who can say no to the design.
